stops.date_confidence: [R] Tradition, and contested; the contradiction is left standing. Savonarolan biography, from Fra Pacifico Burlamacchi onward, has the dying Lorenzo send for Savonarola, who exacts faith and restitution and then withholds absolution when Lorenzo will not restore Florentine liberty. A visit is plausible; the scripted dialogue is not established. Day defaulted to 01.

stops.date_confidence: Attested (Wikipedia, 'Lorenzo de' Medici': died during the late night of 8 April 1492 at the family villa of Careggi, aged 43). The portents are Florentine chronicle tradition and are tagged [R] in the research pool. The retrospective diagnosis of acromegaly, argued by some modern medical historians from his symptoms, his skeleton and his death mask, is explicitly speculative and forms no part of the contemporary record.

stops.date_confidence: Attested (Wikipedia, 'Lorenzo de' Medici'; Wikipedia, 'Sagrestia Vecchia'): first buried alongside Giuliano in the porphyry and bronze tomb chest Verrocchio made for Piero and Giovanni de' Medici between 1469 and 1472, in the Old Sacristy. The day of burial is not given in any source fetched; 9 April is a placeholder to order the segment.

stops.stop: New Sacristy, San Lorenzo, the unmarked chest
stops.date_confidence: Attested (Wikipedia, 'Lorenzo de' Medici'; Wikipedia, 'New Sacristy'): the bodies of Lorenzo and Giuliano were moved into the New Sacristy in 1559 and placed in an unmarked tomb beneath Michelangelo's Madonna and Child. This postdates his life by sixty-seven years and is carried here as the resting place of his own body, not as a journey he made. Month and day defaulted to 01. CORRECTION to the research pool: the installation of the sculptures was Niccolò Tribolo's in 1545, finished by Vasari and Ammannati by 1555, not Vasari's alone.
